prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1477; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Insured vehicle was reversing out of a space when it contacted the rear quarter panel of a parked vehicle. Claimant reports minor back strain after the impact and is currently seeking medical evaluation. Claimant is not represented by an attorney. Initial photos requested from both parties.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes lower back stiffness and pain when bending, with no loss of consciousness and no airbag deployment in either vehicle. Claimant confirms a visit to an urgent care clinic and will forward the discharge notes. Explained the claims process and the bodily injury component of the claim. Claimant has not signed any release.

Entry 3: Received photos of both vehicles. Damage to insured vehicle is limited to the rear bumper cover. Claimant's vehicle shows a dented rear quarter panel and a cracked taillight lens. Parking lot surveillance footage requested from the property manager. Footage confirms insured vehicle was in reverse at low speed and no other vehicles were involved.

Entry 4: Medical discharge notes received. Diagnosis listed as acute lumbar strain, with a recommendation for rest, over-the-counter pain relief, and a follow-up with the claimant's primary care provider if symptoms persist. Claimant has been advised that a physical therapy referral may be needed and that treatment records will be required before the injury portion of the claim can be evaluated.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant. Claimant reports symptoms are improving but has not yet returned to normal activity. Claimant asked whether it is advisable to hire an attorney; informed claimant that legal advice is outside the scope of this adjuster's role and that the claimant may seek independent counsel if desired. Repair estimate for claimant's vehicle is under review, and a file review is scheduled for next week.
